intro.data: Three content types now, chained: a User list becomes an Email list becomes a Domain list. At each type you are handed THREE converters, all the right shape (a List in, an Optional out): safeHead, headOrDefault, and takeLast. Only one family travels cleanly through the chain — gives the same answer whether you transform first and then collapse, or collapse first and then transform. safeHead does. The decoys are typed identically but disagree across the chain. Pick the family that always agrees, at all three types.
intro.alchemy: Three reagents now, chained: a Herb rack becomes an Essence rack becomes a Tincture rack. At each reagent you are handed THREE methods, all the right shape (a rack in, a single vial out): 'Take First', 'First or Conjure', and 'Take Last'. Only one family travels cleanly through the chain — gives the same result whether you refine first and then draw, or draw first and then refine. 'Take First' does. The decoys are shaped identically but disagree across the chain. Pick the family that always agrees, at all three reagents.
intro.spellcraft: Three essences now, chained: a Rune stack becomes a Spark stack becomes an Ember stack. At each essence you are handed THREE workings, all the right shape (a stack in, a single rune out): 'Take Top', 'Top or Conjure', and 'Take Bottom'. Only one family travels cleanly through the chain — gives the same result whether you transform first and then draw, or draw first and then transform. 'Take Top' does. The decoys are shaped identically but disagree across the chain. Choose the family that always agrees, at all three essences.
intro.abstract: Functors F, G : C → D are given, where C is A --f--> B --g--> C. A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is a family of components α_X : F(X) → G(X) such that every naturality square commutes: α_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_A and α_C ∘ F(g) = G(g) ∘ α_B. At each object THREE same-typed candidates are offered; only one family satisfies both squares. Choose it.

goal.data: At all three content types, pick the converter so transform-then-collapse matches collapse-then-transform across the whole chain.
goal.alchemy: At all three reagents, pick the method so refine-then-draw matches draw-then-refine across the whole chain.
goal.spellcraft: At all three essences, choose the working so transform-then-draw matches draw-then-transform across the whole chain.
goal.abstract: Choose components making α_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_A and α_C ∘ F(g) = G(g) ∘ α_B.

afterSuccess.data: safeHead gave the same result both ways around every square — for f and for g — so it travelled cleanly down the whole chain. headOrDefault disagreed (its invented default breaks on the empty list) and takeLast disagreed (a last-picker beside a head-picking neighbour reads different ends of the list). All three had the same type at every object; only safeHead made every square commute. Matching shapes was never enough — agreement on both ends is what makes the whole family natural.
afterSuccess.alchemy: 'Take First' gave the same result both ways around every square — for Extract and for Distil — so it travelled cleanly down the whole chain. 'First or Conjure' disagreed (its conjured vial breaks on the empty rack) and 'Take Last' disagreed (a last-drawer beside a first-drawing neighbour pulls different vials). All three had the same shape at every reagent; only 'Take First' made every square commute. Matching shapes was never enough — agreement on both ends is what makes the whole family natural.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: 'Take Top' gave the same result both ways around every square — for Invoke and for Kindle — so it travelled cleanly down the whole chain. 'Top or Conjure' disagreed (its conjured rune breaks on the empty stack) and 'Take Bottom' disagreed (a bottom-drawer beside a top-drawing neighbour pulls different runes). All three had the same shape at every essence; only 'Take Top' made every square commute. Matching shapes was never enough — agreement on both ends is what makes the whole working natural.
afterSuccess.abstract: Only the safeHead family makes BOTH naturality squares commute (for f and for g). The headOrDefault and takeLast families are correctly typed at every object yet fail at least one square, so neither is a natural transformation. Correct typing is necessary but not sufficient; every square must commute.

reveal.summary: A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is natural only when every naturality square commutes — α_B ∘ F(f) = G(f) ∘ α_A for every f : A → B. With more morphisms there are more squares, and a family must satisfy all of them; agreeing on one square is not enough.
reveal.moreFormal: The engine composes both ways around each square using D's composition table and compares. headOrDefault injects a fixed default and takeLast picks the opposite end; each is well-typed but breaks at least one square, so neither family is natural.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: safeHead<A>: List<A> => Optional<A> is parametric, so it commutes with map for every chained mapping. headOrDefault injects a fixed default (breaking parametricity); takeLast is parametric on its own but, mixed with a head-picking neighbour across a chain, the composed transformations disagree.
